questions.qtext: Which of the following is an exact inference method in Bayesian Networks?
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In variable elimination, factors are multiplied before summing out a variable.
S2 : Variable elimination gives the exact value of posterior probability for the query variable(s), given evidence.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• In variable elimination, we first multiply all factors involving the variable to be eliminated.
Only after this, we perform summation over that variable. This maintains the correctness of marginalization. So, S1 is correct.
• Variable elimination is an exact inference method. It computes the true posterior distribution of the query variable given the observed evidence, without using approximations. So, S2 is correct.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following algorithms is used in Exact Inference methods?
questions.solution:
(d)
• Variational Inference approximates the true distribution by optimizing over a simpler family of distributions, making it a fast but approximate method.
• Gibbs Sampling is an approximate inference method that uses MCMC to draw samples from the posterior distribution. It is useful when exact inference is computationally infeasible.
• Loopy Belief Propagation applies belief propagation in graphs with cycles, but results are only approximate and not guaranteed to converge.
• Belief Propagation performs exact inference in tree-structured Bayesian networks by passing messages between nodes. It guarantees correct marginal probabilities when the graph has no loops.

questions.qtext: Which of the following methods uses random sampling?
questions.solution:
(c)
Monte Carlo methods use random sampling to approximate complex probability distributions.
Other methods like Belief Propagation, Variational Inference, and Variable Elimination do not rely on random sampling.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In a Markov Chain, the future state depends only on the current state and not on any previous states.
S2 : The samples generated before reaching the stationary distribution are called burn-in samples.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• This is the Markov property, where the process is memoryless.
The next state depends solely on the current state, not on how it got there. So, S1 is correct.
• Burn-in samples are early outputs from the Markov chain before it reaches equilibrium.
These samples are discarded to ensure unbiased inference. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Mean-field approximation is more computationally expensive than structured methods.
S2 : Structured variational methods assume all variables are independent.
Which of the following is incorrect?
questions.solution:
(b)
• Mean-field approximation assumes all variables are independent, which simplifies the joint
distribution into a product of marginals. This reduces computational complexity but can sacrifice
accuracy when variables are actually dependent. So, S1 is correct.
• Structured variational methods capture dependencies between variables instead of assuming
independence. This improves accuracy but requires more computation compared to meanfield.
So, S2 is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
I. Gibbs sampling avoids computing the full joint distribution by sampling from the conditional distribution of each variable.
II. Gibbs sampling always converges quickly, even when the variables are highly correlated.
III. In Gibbs sampling, each variable is sampled conditionally on the current values of all other variables.
How many of the above statements are correct?

NAT
questions.solution:
2
• Gibbs sampling is a type of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method.
It avoids computing the full joint distribution by sampling each variable from its conditional
distribution, keeping all other variables fixed. So, Statement I is correct.
• Gibbs sampling does not always converge quickly.
If variables are highly correlated, the Markov chain may mix slowly, leading to slow
convergence. So, Statement II is incorrect.
• In Gibbs sampling, each variable is indeed sampled conditionally, based on the current values
of all other variables. This is the core mechanism of the algorithm. So, Statement III is correct.

questions.qtext: In a Bayesian Network, what does the Conditional Probability Table (CPT) for a node represent?

options.text: The marginal probability of the node.
The joint probability of all nodes in the network.
The probability of the node given its parents.
The frequency count of the node values.

questions.solution:
(c)
Each node has a CPT specifying its probability distribution conditioned on its parent nodes.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: Loopy Belief Propagation always converges when the network contains cycles.
Variational Inference can optimize the ELBO.
The Junction Tree algorithm is also known as the Clique Tree algorithm.

questions.solution:
(b, c)
• Loopy Belief Propagation is not guaranteed to converge in graphs with cycles.
Even if it converges, the results are approximate and may not represent the true marginals.
So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Variational Inference converts inference into an optimization problem by maximizing the
Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO).
This approach approximates the true posterior distribution with a simpler distribution. So,
option (b) is correct.
• The Junction Tree algorithm is also called the Clique Tree algorithm.
It converts the graph into a tree of cliques to enable exact inference efficiently. So, option (c)
is correct.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In a junction tree, each node (clique) contains a subset of variables that form a complete (fully connected) subgraph.
S2 : Junction tree representation is used to perform exact inference by propagating messages between cliques.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Each node in a junction tree corresponds to a maximal clique from a triangulated graph, where all variables in the clique are fully connected. So, S1 is correct.
• Junction trees are used for exact inference through message passing between cliques, enabling efficient marginal and conditional probability computations. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following best describes the burn-in period in Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods?

options.text: The initial samples that are discarded before the Markov chain reaches the stationary distribution.
The final samples taken after the stationary distribution is reached.
Samples drawn directly from the target distribution.
Samples used to initialize the Markov chain randomly.

questions.solution:
(a)
• Burn-in samples are discarded to avoid the bias from the early phase of the Markov chain.
This ensures only samples from the stationary phase are used. So, option (a) is correct.
• Final samples are retained and used for analysis, not discarded. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• In MCMC, we sample indirectly via the Markov chain, not directly from the target distribution.
Hence, So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Initialization refers to the starting point of the chain.
It is unrelated to the definition of the burn-in period. So, option (d) is incorrect.

options.text: The elimination of a variable involves summing over its values in the joint factor where it appears.
Introducing evidence in variable elimination means conditioning the relevant factors on observed values.
The complexity of variable elimination is independent of the elimination ordering.
Variable elimination can generate intermediate factors with more variables than any original CPT.

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
• Eliminating a variable means summing over its values in the product of all relevant factors.
So, option (a) is correct.
• Observing evidence modifies the factors by conditioning-only values consistent with the
evidence are retained. So, option (b) is correct.
• The order of elimination matters. A poor order may lead to large intermediate factors and
increased complexity. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• During elimination, multiplying factors can result in intermediate factors involving more
variables than any original CPT, leading to higher computation. So, option (d) is correct.
